metaDescription: Rotate all pages or a chosen range of a PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise, adding to any existing rotation. Free, in your browser.
intro: Rotate every page, or just a range, of a PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise and save the result as a new file.
why:
A scan that came out sideways, a landscape table in a portrait report or an upside-down page from a document feeder is a daily annoyance. Viewers can rotate the display, but the change is lost the moment you send the file on.

This tool writes the rotation into the PDF itself. Choose a clockwise angle of 90, 180 or 270 degrees and, if you like, a page range such as 2,4-6, or leave it blank for all pages. The rotation is added to whatever each page already has, so rotating a page that is already turned 90 degrees by 90 more makes 180. The page content is not re-rendered or changed, only its orientation flag. Encrypted files are refused. The work happens in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Enter a page range such as 2,4-6, or leave it blank to rotate all pages.
Run the tool and download the rotated PDF.

faq.a: Use 270 degrees for a quarter turn counter-clockwise, because 270 clockwise is the same thing. For a half turn, 180 is the same in either direction.

faq.q: Does it stack on existing rotation?
faq.a: Yes. The new angle is added to each page's current rotation and wrapped at 360. A page already rotated 90 degrees and turned another 90 ends at 180.
No. Only the page's rotation value is changed, so text stays sharp and searchable and file size is nearly the same. Nothing is re-rendered.

faq.q: Can I rotate pages by an arbitrary angle?
faq.a: No. PDF page rotation works in steps of 90 degrees only. Straightening a slightly skewed scan needs an image editor.
